title: MLS Predictions: Fierce Battles Ignite Opening Round of the 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Zach Lowy6:00 PM ESTMLS Cup playoffs kick off this week. / Mark Thorstenson/Orlando City/MLS/Getty Images (Griezmann); Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images (Union); Tanner Pearson/Getty Images (Nashville)While 12 Major League Soccer teams have bid farewell to the 2026 season, there are still 18 alive and in pursuit of the ultimate prize: the 2026 MLS Cup.
Postseason action kicks off on Thursday with the two wild card matches, while the multiple Round One best-of-three series will take place from Saturday onwards.
The stakes could not possibly be higher. Out of the 18 teams competing in the playoffs, nine have never lifted the MLS Cup.
Here, Sports Illustrated dives into how it all may play out.

Kévin Denkey holds the key to Cincinnati progressing to the opening round. / Tanner Pearson/Getty ImagesDate: Thursday, Nov. 19Time: 7:30 p.m. ET / 4:30 p.m. PTOrlando City went into the World Cup break on a 6–2 loss to Cincinnati, leaving them 12th in the Eastern Conference. However, with World Cup winner Antoine Griezmann joining their ranks later that summer, Orlando have managed to turn things around and qualify for the postseason.

They are still vulnerable at the back, having conceded two-plus goals in eight of their last 10 matches, and there’s reason to believe that Evander and Kévin Denkey can take advantage of their defensive frailties and find the back of the net in Florida. Therefore, All signs point to this one being an attacking shootout between two sides that will be putting it all on the line over the course of 90+ minutes.

Nevertheless, the Lions have enjoyed a superb run of form at Inter&Co Stadium, taking 19 points from a possible 21 in their last seven home matches. We're expecting that impressive home form to continue on Thursday, with Griezmann leading the squad to victory to set up a mouthwatering opening round clash with Nashville SC.
Score Prediction: Orlando City 4–3 FC Cincinnati

Seattle Sounders have snuck into the postseason at the last second, but can they extend their run? / Alika Jenner/MLS/Getty ImagesDate: Thursday, Nov.19Time: 10:00 p.m. ET / 7:00 p.m. PTSeattle Sounders entered Decision Day in a miserable state with just two points from their previous five matches. But after edging LAFC on Decision Day, they have snuck into the playoffs at the very last second. They’ll be hosting Real Salt Lake, who will enter on four wins in their last five.

While Real Salt Lake have overachieved following the losses of key players like Diego Luna and Zavier Gozo, they have struggled at Lumen Field, losing three of four and drawing the other. In contrast to RSL, who have lost in the opening round of the last four playoffs, Seattle have playoff success in their DNA. We’re expecting Brian Schmetzer’s side to come out on top in the Emerald City.
Score Prediction: Seattle Sounders 1–0 Real Salt Lake

Center back Neil Pierre has been a primary reason for the Union’s resurgence. / Carly Mackler/Getty ImagesDate: Saturday, Nov. 21Time: 2:00 p.m. ET / 11:00 a.m. PTHaving lost their last six matches against Philadelphia Union, New England turned things around in May with a comeback 2–1 win against the Union. Five months later, they won 2–1 in Pennsylvania, snapping Philadelphia’s club-record 15-match unbeaten streak.

After a red-hot run of form, Philadelphia cooled off with two points from four matches before beating Toronto on Decision Day. New England, meanwhile, have lost two in a row going into the postseason. There’s not a great deal between the two, but we’re expecting home advantage to power the Revs to a hard-fought win.
Score Prediction: New England Revolution in three

FC Dallas are looking to return to the Western Conference semifinals for the first time in four years. / Omar Vega/Getty ImagesDate: Saturday, Nov. 21Time: 4:00 p.m. ET / 1:00 p.m. PTPortland Timbers have found their form at the right time, winning their last four to sneak into the seventh position. However, they’re going to have their hands full as they look to make it past FC Dallas.

Dallas haven’t lost to Portland since 2023, and they haven’t lost at home to the Timbers since 2018. Having won each of their last three home meetings against Portland, they should be capable of getting the job done and sealing their spot in the Western Conference semifinals.

Columbus Crew are looking to pull off an upset against the defending champions. / Harry Figiel/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesDate: Saturday, Nov. 21Time: 6:00 p.m. ET / 3:00 p.m. PTInter Miami are looking to become the first team in 14 years to successfully defend the MLS Cup, but first, they'll have to get past the most in-form team in MLS: Columbus Crew. In just two months, Columbus have picked themselves up from the cellar of the Eastern Conference and climbed into seventh place after winning six in a row.

Miami, in contrast, have struggled to maintain consistency over a season that has seen them go through three different managers. They’ve been handicapped defensively, conceding two-plus goals in three of their last four matches.

Moreover, they’ve been particularly vulnerable in the final minutes. After conceding an 84th-minute equalizer to Columbus’s Brais Méndez in a 2–2 draw back in August, Miami then conceded a last-second game-winner to Columbus’s Jamal Thiaré in September’s 2–1 result. The Herons also squandered a three-goal lead and ended 3–3 with Charlotte FC on Decision Day.
